name: Posteromedial approach to the talus
corridor: Incision between the Achilles and the medial malleolus, identifying FHL as the most posterior structure and working lateral to FHL so the tendon and posterior tibial bundle retract together

positioning.text: Position so the interval between the Achilles and the medial malleolus can be imaged over the subtalar joint and a tibia–calcaneus distractor can be applied.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the Achilles tendon, medial malleolus, and the expected posterior tibial bundle behind the malleolus. Center the cut over the subtalar joint; fluoroscopy can guide placement.

incision.text: Incise between the Achilles laterally and the medial malleolus medially, with the exact line set by the patient's anatomy.

superficial_interval.text: Protect the neurovascular structures that run behind the medial malleolus. Identify FHL, the most posterior structure, and dissect posterior and laterally, remaining medial to the Achilles.

deep_interval.text: Deepen lateral to FHL and open its sheath if needed so FHL and the posterior tibial bundle retract together, exposing the fracture. FHL travels between two tubercles on the posterior talar body; fractures through that groove can use FHL as a reduction clue. Do not work so far proximal that the distal tibia is mistaken for the talus.

layers.text: Skin, posterior tibial neurovascular plane, FHL, then the posterior talar body and the posterior tibiotalar and talocalcaneal joints.

structures_at_risk.text: The posterior tibial neurovascular bundle lies directly in this approach behind the medial malleolus and must be protected throughout.

danger_zones.text: Working medial to FHL or dissecting behind the medial malleolus without identifying the bundle is the danger zone.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract FHL together with the bundle rather than separating them, and avoid closing in a way that constricts the bundle.

exposure.text: Shows posteromedial talar-body and posterior-process fractures and only the posterior tibiotalar and posterior talocalcaneal joints. A distractor between tibia and calcaneus can help.

limitations.text: Does not show the anterior half of the talar body.

indications.text: Used for posteromedial talar-body or posterior-process fractures.

closure.text: Close in layers, reconstructing the deep structures without compromising the posterior tibial bundle.

complications.text: Complications include posterior tibial neurovascular injury and mistaking the distal tibia for the talus if the dissection is too proximal.

procedure_applications.condition: A posteromedial talar-body or posterior-process fracture is reduced; FHL in the intertubercle groove can guide the reduction

questions.question: What is the most posterior structure used to find the interval?
questions.answer: Flexor hallucis longus; work lateral to it so the tendon and the posterior tibial bundle retract together.

questions.question: How can FHL help reduce a posterior talar-body fracture?
questions.answer: FHL runs in the intertubercle groove; that relationship can guide reduction of fragments through the groove.

questions.question: What proximal pitfall must be avoided?
questions.answer: Working too far proximal and mistaking the distal tibia for the talus.
